fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 -shuffle=on ./internal/api -run "^($(grep -l newSessionFixture internal/api/*_test.go | xargs grep -ho '^func Test[A-Za-z0-9_]*' | cut -c6- | paste -sd'|'))\$" (every test in the files that call newSessionFixture) passes twice in a row with different shuffle seeds, and the same run with -race reports no data race; grep shows no t.Setenv left in newSessionFixture and TestMain in internal/api/budget_test.go sets XDG_CACHE_HOME and removes the folder when the binary exits; go vet ./internal/api is clean. Failure case: a session-fixture test that starts a run step or inspects run-tmp stays serial with a comment saying why, and no test writes under the host's ~/.cache. Touches internal/api/budget_test.go, session_test.go's newSessionFixture and the _test.go files that call newSessionFixture only. Must not skip, delete or merge a test: go test -list '.*' ./internal/api counts the same tests as before. Must not change non-test code.
fields.statement: internal/api's TestMain (in budget_test.go) points XDG_CACHE_HOME at one temporary folder for the whole test binary and newSessionFixture stops calling t.Setenv, and the tests in the _test.go files that call newSessionFixture call t.Parallel(); among them a test that swaps a package variable (runClock, daemonTicker, daemonReexec and the like), calls t.Setenv or t.Chdir, uses run temp folders, or reads shared machine state stays serial, and a comment on each such test says why it must.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 -shuffle=on ./internal/api -run "^($(grep -L newSessionFixture internal/api/daemon_*_test.go internal/api/run_*_test.go internal/api/ship_*_test.go internal/api/watchdog_*_test.go internal/api/health_*_test.go internal/api/usage_*_test.go internal/api/feed_*_test.go | xargs grep -ho '^func Test[A-Za-z0-9_]*' | cut -c6- | paste -sd'|'))\$" (every test in those files) passes twice in a row with different shuffle seeds; go vet ./internal/api is clean. Failure case: go test -trimpath -race -count=1 ./internal/api with the same -run pattern (the daemonTicker, daemonReexec, webFactory, pollGitTimeout and runClock swappers, run_handback_test.go's and run_spawned_test.go's tests, beside the parallel ones) reports no data race. Touches only the _test.go files of those prefixes that do not call newSessionFixture. Must not skip, delete or merge a test: go test -list '.*' ./internal/api counts the same tests as before. Must not change non-test code.
fields.statement: The tests in internal/api's daemon_, run_, ship_, watchdog_, health_, usage_ and feed_ _test.go files that do not call newSessionFixture call t.Parallel() when independent; a test that swaps a package variable (runClock, daemonTicker, daemonReexec and the like), calls t.Setenv or t.Chdir, uses run temp folders, or reads shared machine state stays serial, and a comment on each such test says why it must.

fields.acceptance: go test -trimpath -count=1 -shuffle=on ./internal/api -skip '^(TestReadBudget|TestReadBudgetApply|TestDriverPollIsCheap)$' passes twice in a row with different shuffle seeds; go vet ./internal/api is clean. Failure case: go test -trimpath -race -count=1 ./internal/api -skip '^(TestReadBudget|TestReadBudgetApply|TestDriverPollIsCheap)$' reports no data race, and a test of these files that sets its own XDG_CACHE_HOME or touches run-tmp (inbox_gate_budget_test.go, slice_test.go, web_actions_test.go and the like) stays serial with a comment saying why. Speedup measure (orchestrator, quiet VM): /usr/bin/time -f '%e s' go test -trimpath -count=1 ./internal/api -skip '^(TestReadBudget|TestReadBudgetApply|TestDriverPollIsCheap)$' within 150 s (2026-11-15: 388 s). Touches only internal/api _test.go files outside the other two leaves' sets. Must not skip, delete or merge a test: go test -list '.*' ./internal/api counts the same tests as before. Must not change non-test code.
fields.statement: The remaining internal/api tests (the _test.go files neither api-tests-parallel-session nor api-tests-parallel-runtime covers: web_, inbox_, rex_, model, change, slice and the rest) call t.Parallel() when independent; a test that swaps a package variable (runClock, daemonTicker, daemonReexec and the like), calls t.Setenv or t.Chdir, uses run temp folders, or reads shared machine state stays serial, and a comment on each such test says why it must; and the whole package then passes shuffled, under -race and within the wall-time target.
